editorial:
Imagine being a retired dad who just wants to see his kids, only to have them all bail on you at the same time. That is where you find Frank, a sweet and lonely guy who discovers his children have been lying to him about how great their lives are. You will feel for him as he hits the road to find them, hoping to fix things and get the truth. The movie has a very cozy, warm feeling, like a long conversation with an old friend. It is not a loud or flashy film, but it hits you right in the heart by showing how parents and children often hide their struggles just to make each other happy.

Robert De Niro does a great job playing a gentle father instead of his usual tough-guy roles. The pacing is steady and relaxed, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a thriller. You will love the honest moments where the family finally stops pretending. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quiet night in. It is a perfect pick for a rainy Sunday when you just want a good cry and a reminder to call your parents.
endingExplained: After visiting everyone, Frank realizes his kids were only lying because they wanted him to be proud of them. He tells them that he loves them no matter what their jobs or bank accounts look like. The movie ends with the whole family finally coming together and being honest. They stop pretending to be perfect and start being a real family again, showing that love is more important than success.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family stories and emotional dramas.
